definitions.explanation: A temporary outdoor shop or stall, commonly seen at festivals, markets, and events.

examples.japanese: {祭|まつ}りで{露店|ろてん}が{並|なら}んでいた。
examples.english: Street stalls lined up at the festival.

examples.japanese: {露店|ろてん}で{焼|や}きそばを{買|か}った。
examples.english: I bought yakisoba from a street stall.

examples.japanese: {神社|じんじゃ}の{参道|さんどう}には{様々|さまざま}な{露店|ろてん}が{出|で}ていた。
examples.english: Various street stalls were set up along the approach to the shrine.

notes:
SIMILAR WORDS:
- {屋台|やたい}: also means street stall/food cart (more common term)
- {出店|でみせ}: vendor stall at an event
- {店|みせ}: general word for shop

COMMON FESTIVAL STALLS:
- {焼|や}きそば (fried noodles)
- たこ{焼|や}き (takoyaki)
- りんご{飴|あめ} (candy apples)
- {金魚|きんぎょ}すくい (goldfish scooping)
- {射的|しゃてき} (shooting gallery)

{露店|ろてん} literally means 'dew shop,' referring to being exposed to the elements.
